cars.generation: Original 1960s GT40 production-road family, represented by Mk III street coupe
cars.variant: Mk III — 1967 Petersen MK3 1105 custodian reference, left-hand drive
cars.specification_market: 1967 GT40 Mk III street coupe, selected Petersen Automotive Museum reference MK3 1105: 289-cu-in V8, 306 bhp, left-hand drive and ZF five-speed manual documented in its earlier museum spotlight. Count the original GT40 road programme once, including original Mk I road cars and Mk III; not extra entries for chassis, years or steering positions. Separate from the 2005 Ford GT, 2017 Ford GT and modern track Mk IV. No Mk II/Mk IV 7.0-litre racing engine, continuation, replica or restoration-specific race tune. British development/build under Ford’s Anglo-American programme; origin United Kingdom does not deny American backing. Other Mk III chassis histories are context, not this car’s build history. No torque/peak speeds, dimensions, mass, production total, price or measured performance assigned.
cars.summary: The original GT40 road programme translated a defining Anglo-American endurance-racing design into an exceptional road sports car. The Petersen and Shelby American Collection document the purpose-built Mk III street version and its historical importance. This entry represents the original road family once; victories by racing GT40 variants are not attributed to the Mk III.

sources.title: 1967 Ford GT40 MK III — collection reference MK3 1105
sources.notes: Relevant full history, chassis identity and quick specifications read. Identifies street-legal MK3 1105, 289-cu-in V8, 306 bhp, left-hand drive, round headlights and extended luggage deck. Historical racing context does not make this Mk III a Le Mans winner. Top speed, acceleration, production counts, price and nominal 40-inch name derivation are not imported as exact technical measurements.

sources.title: 1966 Ford GT40 M3/1102 — Mk III street coupe
sources.source_type: Direct collection custodian history, separate chassis context
sources.notes: Relevant complete Details & History read. Documents a separate Mk III completed late 1966, not the selected Petersen 1967 car. No 1102 power/torque peak or individual history copied into 1105. The page’s assertion that Mk III is the only street GT40 is not adopted: original Mk I road cars also belong to the duplicate boundary. No direct factory-literature inspection claimed.

media.caption: Mk III GT40 displayed at the National Motor Museum, Beaulieu, photographed by sv1ambo and titled 1969 Ford GT40 Mk III. Individually inspected frontal view shows the Mk III’s round lamps and road-car body. This right-hand-drive display car is representative imagery, not the selected Petersen left-hand-drive MK3 1105 or authentication of its engine, gearbox, build year or originality. A separate photographed display placard is not used as technical evidence.
